# Format fixture corpus

This directory contains synthetic data used to preserve Cellularity's immutable
Java-format compatibility contract.

- `FormatFixtureCorpus.cpp` is the deterministic generator and verifier.
- `corpus/manifest.tsv` records every legacy version axis, compression mode, object counts,
  expected semantic markers, compatibility branch IDs, provenance, license, and SHA-256.
- Files below `corpus` contain generated bytes only. They contain no user names,
  paths, device identifiers, or imported user data.

All corpus files are generated specifically for Cellularity and distributed under
the repository MIT license. No historical user substrate or genome file is included.
`compression=none` means the bytes are stored directly. `split-java-gzip` is the
legacy v13+ layout: an uncompressed Java primitive-stream header followed by a
gzip-compressed Java primitive-stream body.

The corpus deliberately contains no discarded pre-release native formats. Release
CLTY golden files live in `testdata/release-format` and are owned by the release
codec tests.

The manifest SHA-256 pins every committed legacy file. Reproducibility checks compare
uncompressed fixtures byte-for-byte; for `split-java-gzip` they compare the exact
prefix and decompressed body because valid DEFLATE output can differ between zlib
implementations.

The standard native test command builds the tool and verifies every manifest entry:

```bash
scripts/native/test.sh
```

Regenerate only after an intentional format-metadata change:

```bash
/tmp/cellularity_native_clang_build/cellularity_format_fixture_tool \
  --generate native/tests/fixtures/corpus
```

Use `--verify` with the same path to verify the committed corpus. Generation is
allowed only when format metadata intentionally changes.
